topic: The Curious Link: Block Collisions and the Digits of Pi
target_audience: High school students interested in physics and mathematics

outline.topic: The Curious Link: Block Collisions and the Digits of Pi
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in physics and mathematics

sections.title: Introduction: The Impossible Connection
sections.content: Hook the audience by posing the counter-intuitive question: How can a mechanical physics experiment involving simple blocks calculate the transcendental number π?
sections.example: Visualize two blocks sliding on a frictionless surface towards a wall; we count the total number of collisions between the blocks and the wall.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Establish the foundational rules: Momentum and Kinetic Energy are conserved in elastic collisions. Introduce the 'Phase Space' concept—representing velocity states as coordinates on a graph.
sections.example: A 1kg block moving at 1m/s hits a 100kg stationary block. Show a vector diagram where the velocity vectors form a circle arc in the 'Configuration Space'.

sections.title: The Geometric Transformation
sections.content: Explain that the collision condition (block-to-block or block-to-wall) maps directly to the reflection of a trajectory inside a wedge-shaped region in the phase plane. The angle of the wedge depends on the ratio of the block masses.
sections.example: Animated visualization of the trajectory bouncing off the walls of a V-shaped region, where the wedge angle is exactly arcsin(sqrt(m1/m2)).

sections.title: The Pi Emergence
sections.content: Demonstrate that as the mass of the second block increases (m2 = 100^n), the total number of collisions between the two blocks and the wall converges to the digits of π. For m2 = 100^k, the number of collisions is the first k+1 digits of π.
sections.example: Side-by-side animation: Block 1 (small) and Block 2 (100kg) collide 3 times. Change Block 2 to 10,000kg, and the animation shows 31 total collisions.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize that this works because the geometry of the phase-space wedge is isomorphic to a circle. The collisions act like a 'discrete' way of measuring an angle, effectively 'discretizing' the ratio of circumference to diameter.
sections.example: Show a summary graphic: Collision Count Table matching 3, 31, 314... as masses scale exponentially, closing with a 'Mind-Blown' visual of blocks forming the π symbol.
